description: The 'bounds' field describes a structural argument ('canonical_digest only takes &WorkflowSource') rather than concrete test input bounds. The obligation description itself acknowledges the test may be a 'structural code review confirmation' rather than a proptest with generated inputs. For P1 this is acceptable because the function signature structurally guarantees the property, but the bounds description should clarify whether this is a true proptest or a code-review checklist item.
recommendation: Either (a) reclassify as static-analysis with structural bounds, or (b) define concrete proptest strategies that exercise AST vs IR distinction with clear input bounds.

description: The agent-invocation-ledger.jsonl tracks only femdation setup. There is no separate proof-planner invocation entry distinguishing the planner from the rust-contract agent that generated the upstream contract artifacts. The STATE.md says 'State: 3 (rust-contract complete)' and the proof-planning artifacts (proof-strategy.md, verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl, proof-obligations.planned.jsonl) were generated without a traceable planner invocation ID. For P1 this is not blocking but should be corrected for full provenance traceability.
recommendation: Add a proof-planner invocation entry to agent-invocation-ledger.jsonl with a distinct planner_invocation_id. Update verifier-lane-decisions.jsonl and proof-obligations.planned.jsonl to reference this planner ID.

description: The bounds field says 'Compile-time enumeration of all current ScalarValue variants' but the obligation is implemented as a runtime unit test (cargo test --lib), not a compile-time assertion. The bounds description conflates the desired outcome (compile-time enforcement of exhaustiveness) with the actual mechanic (runtime test that breaks when variants are added). The distinction matters because the test does not prevent compilation if a new variant is added — it only fails at test time.
recommendation: Clarify in bounds field that this is a runtime test asserting that the _ arm is unreachable for current variants. Note that it does NOT provide compile-time enforcement; true compile-time enforcement would require removing the _ arm.

description: All three Kani harnesses use a tracking mock for blake3::Hasher rather than real blake3. This is a legitimate model reduction (proving input discrimination rather than hash correctness) documented in trusted-base-plan.md (S-1). The proof-writer must implement the mock such that it is a faithful abstraction: the mock must record byte sequences in order exactly as they would be fed to real blake3. If the mock diverges from real update() semantics, the proof becomes vacuously true.
recommendation: Proof-writer must: (a) implement the mock to track update() calls in order with exact byte content, (b) document the mock as a trusted stub in the harness file, (c) ensure proptest defense-in-depth exercises the real blake3 path to catch any mock/reality divergence.

description: Waiver WC-002 ('_ arm producing b"unsupported"') is marked behavior_affecting: true. The waiver waives a contract clause (C8) that explicitly permits the current behavior — so the waiver acknowledges a known gap rather than hiding one. PO-STATIC-FINISH-001 provides compensating evidence. For P1 this is acceptable because the current ScalarValue enum has only 2 variants, both explicitly handled.
recommendation: No action needed for this bead. Track WC-002 expiry (2027-05-24) and ensure PO-STATIC-FINISH-001 is maintained when new ScalarValue variants are added.
